svg.title: PromptVault FHE key-gate mechanic — what the chain sees vs what the browser sees
svg.desc: Shows the two euint128 key handles stored on-chain, the CoFHE ACL granting buyer access on payment, the Threshold Network enforcing the ACL, and how the plaintext key only ever exists in the browser.

g.onclick: sendPrompt('What does the PromptVault contract store on-chain?')
sendPrompt('How does the CoFHE ACL record buyer access in PromptVault?')
sendPrompt('How does the Threshold Network enforce ACL in PromptVault?')
g.text: Checks ACL before decrypting key parts

g.onclick: sendPrompt('What happens in the buyers browser in PromptVault?')
sendPrompt('What is stored on IPFS in PromptVault?')
g.text: Public, but useless without the FHE-gated key

svg.text: 🔒 On-chain: only ciphertexts. Chain sees 0x4f8a… not "You are a senior Solidity auditor…"
✅ ACL is cryptographic, not just a require() check — Threshold Network enforces it
🚫 allowPublic is never called — no code path reaches it
